figures.caption: Fig. 12 Predicted fragment lipid content distributions for the models with linear lipid-dependent death (a) and exponential time-dependent death (b). The negative-binomial fragment lipid content distributions corresponding to the MLE values of µf and cvf are overlaid on the posterior predictions, which are shown in transparent blue. The monotone decrease in both cases reflects a weighting towards the uptake of smaller fragments.

Fig. C.1 A prior distribution for η̂, based on previous experiments [18]. Plot (a) shows the prior distribution for η̂ and plot (b) the associated half-clearance time of apoptotic material if the initial macrophage density is sustained. Both distributions are lognormal and defined so that the half-clearance time of apoptotic material has mode 1.5 h, in accordance with the results in [18], and 97.5% quantile at 12 h, substantially longer than established minutesto-hours timescales [15, 29].

Fig. 9 The AIC-preferred model when fitting directly to the lipid distribution over 0 < t ≤ 48. The plots above illustrate the MLE for the fragmented uptake model with saturating time-dependent death (Eqs. (32) and (33), β1[1 + (β1/β0 − 1)e−t/q ]−1 ). The experimental data are overlaid. Plot (a) shows the cell population M̂(t) with 95% observation windows shaded and plot (b) the mean ingested lipid per cell L̂M (t). Plots (c) and (d) show the predicted lipid distributions, m̂ℓ(t), on linear and log-linear axes, respectively. Note how, relative to Fig. 8, this model produces an improved fit for m̂ℓ(t) slightly at the expense of L̂M (t). The parameter values are: µe = 54.7, µf = 15.4, cvf = 1.90, β0 = 1.02 × 10−3, β1 = 0.0337, q = 8.33, σM = 0.120 and σm = 0.0893.
Fig. 3 Schematics for the three uptake mechanisms considered in this paper.

Fig. 10 Models parametrised under the rapid efferocytosis assumption (η̂ → ∞) cannot capture the full data 0 ≤ t ≤ 60 when η̂ is made finite. The plots show solutions to Eqs. (29)-(31) with saturating, time-dependent death for η̂ = 0.01, 0.1, 1. The remaining parameter values are listed in Fig. 9 and are consistent with the fit for η̂ → ∞ over 0 < t ≤ 48. Plot (a) displays the predicted mean ingested lipid per cell and plot (b) the total cell lipid, defined in Eq. (1). Experimental data are overlaid, assuming µe = 54.7 in plot (b). Note that decreases to η̂ reduce macrophage lipid content, but not in a manner consistent with the data.

Fig. A.2 Fits for the AIC-preferred whole-cell uptake model in Table 2. The plots depict solutions to Eqs. (15)-(16) for βℓ = β0eβ1t with respect to the pseudo-likelihood (44). Note the predicted local maxima in plots (c) and (d) at t = 36 and t = 48 that are not observed in the data. Parameter values are listed in Table B.2.

Fig. A.3 Fits for the fragmented uptake model with linear, lipid-dependent death listed in Table 2. The plots depict solutions to Eqs. (32)-(33) for βℓ = β0 +β1ℓ with respect to the pseudo-likelihood (44). Parameter values are listed in Table B.2.

Fig. A.1 The MLE (42) derived by assuming all lipid distribution observations are independent can bias the fit towards m̂ℓ(t) at the expense of M̂(t). The consistent underestimate for M̂(t) in plot (a) for all 0 < t ≤ 60 casts doubt on the validity of the fit as a faithful representation of the dynamics underlying the data. This example shows the MLE for the fragmented uptake model (29)-(31) with βℓ = β0+β1ℓ. The parameter values are: η̂ = 1.0, µe = 27, µf = 31, cvf = 2.0, β0 = 0.0053, β1 = 0.0022, σM = 0.68 and σm = 0.080.

Fig. A.4 Fits for the fragmented uptake model with exponential, timedependent death listed in Table 3. The plots depict solutions to Eqs. (29)-(31) for βℓ = β0eβ1t with respect to the pseudo-likelihood (44). Parameter values are listed in Table B.3.

Fig. 2 The possible trajectories of the total macrophage lipid content depend on mean endogenous lipid content, µe. Plot (a) shows the normalised total macrophage lipid content LM (t)/LM (0), defined in Eq. (1), when the data for total macrophage count M(t) and mean ingested lipid content L̂M (t) are substituted. The chosen values of µe illustrate the three qualitatively distinct possible trajectories. Plot (b) shows the deviance from one across 0 ≤ t ≤ 48, as defined in Eq. (2). Note the single minimum at µe ≈ 42.6 where these data are collinear within D(µe) < 2× 10−3.
